newsitem.title: UK: UK unit trust sales steady despite market nerves.
newsitem.headline: UK unit trust sales steady despite market nerves.

text.p: July net UK retail unit trust sales, net Personal Equity Plan (PEP) sales and net corporate bond sales were stable despite volatile world markets, data from the AUTIF released on Wednesday showed.
But total net unit trust investment in July, including both retail and institutional sales, dropped to 616 million stg from 722 million stg the month before.
"This was essentially due to a number of institutional managers moving away from international markets," the Association of Unit Trusts and Investment Funds (AUTIF) said.

Of net retail sales in July of 419 million stg (previous 421 million stg), the bias was 85 percent towards the UK. Sales of Europe funds halved from last month and Far East funds plunged to just 5.0 million stg from 37 million stg the month before.

Institutional sales in July concentrated on growth funds, split between 172 million in the International Growth sector, 98 million stg in UK Growth, 43 million stg in UK Growth and Income and 13 million stg in UK Smaller Companies.
"The only other sector to have made a positive impression on the total was the Fund of Funds sector which added sales of 82 million stg," AUTIF said.
The Investment Trusts Units sector with net sales of 24 million stg, reached their highest level ever and reflected the recent interest in take-overs, the association added.

North America was the least favoured destination for unit trust funds in July for the third month in succession. Retail investors pulled out 55 million and institutional investors a further 123 million stg.
